finalText:
Migration complete. All 78 JS files pass `node --check`.

## What changed

12 files were still on `db.query(sql, params)` — 36 call sites, converted to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `service/teamService.js`, `repo/session.js` |
| analytics | `repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `service/couponService.js`, `repo/refund.js` |
| catalog | `admin/variantAdmin.js`, `repo/supplier.js` |
| orders | `service/returnService.js`, `repo/shipment.js` |
| support | `admin/macroAdmin.js`, `repo/sla.js` |

Each file had the same three-call shape (get-by-id / list / update), matching the already-migrated siblings like `support/src/repo/macro.js` line-for-line. Counts confirm the sweep is complete: 225 `db.execute(` call sites = 75 caller files × 3, with the only non-callers being `lib/db.js`, `lib/cache.js`, and the vendor adapter.

## Two things I deliberately left alone

**`vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9,13`** — the last two `db.query` calls in the repo. The file header says:

> Vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4. Do not edit — it is replaced wholesale on every upgrade, and local changes are silently lost.

Editing it would migrate cleanly but get reverted on the next vendor bump, so this needs a real fix rather than a sweep: upstream the change to legacy-orm, wrap the adapter behind a shim that translates positional→object form, or drop the dependency. Worth deciding before the driver's next major actually removes `query`, since these two calls will break at that point. Tell me which route you want and I'll do it.

**25 `cache.query(...)` calls** (line 18 of each `repo/*.js`) — same method name, different object. `lib/cache.js` has its own `query`, unrelated to the db migration, so a naive find-and-replace on `.query(` would have broken all 25.
